chunks: A shaykh of the people of Ray called Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Saqr al-Sa'igh al-'Adl narrated this hadith to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Abbas b. Bassam narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Abi al-Haytham al-Sa'di narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to me. He said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us from his father, from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, from Abdullah b. Abbas,
[a hadith] similar to that, except that he said in his hadith: A meteor falls from the sky at sunrise, and it lands in the house of one of you.

key_terms.بمثل ذلك: Similarly to that — indicates this is a variant narration of the preceding hadith
key_terms.كوكب: Meteor or shooting star — a celestial sign
key_terms.يهوي: Falls/descends — a cosmic event signifying divine designation

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about a meteor falling from the sky at sunrise as a sign of the designated successor?
ai.summary: This is a variant narration of the previous hadith about a celestial sign marking the divinely chosen successor. Transmitted through a chain including Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, Imam al-Baqir, and Imam Zayn al-Abidin back to Ibn Abbas, the narrator reports the same tradition but with the variant wording that the meteor falls 'at sunrise' rather than 'at the break of dawn,' and lands 'in the house of one of you.' The slight variation in wording is typical of hadith transmission across different chains.
